packageRules.description: React/Next: framework surface, kept in one reviewed group.

Trade-off 119 (issue #529): no TypeScript 7 yet. typescript-eslint 8.70 supports TypeScript <6.1 and needs the compiler API that TypeScript 7 does not ship; the type-aware promise rules (issue #517) depend on it. Remove once a typescript-eslint release supports TypeScript 7.
TypeScript/ESLint: kept in one reviewed group.
Playwright/browser tooling: kept in one reviewed group so the pinned Chromium build and the MCP server move together.
Accessibility tooling: kept in one reviewed group.
Issue #252: majors on providers/engines with real behavior or cost risk stay manual - never automerged, never grouped away from a dedicated review.
The regex-tracked pins (restic, the local Renovate image, agent tooling) have no digest capture group, so they stay pinned by version, not digest.
Issue #252: automerge only dev-only patch updates, and only after every required CI check passes.
Everything else (runtime deps, and every minor/major not covered above) stays a reviewed PR by default.

customManagers.description: Issues #252 and #485: .mcp.json and .codex/config.toml pin the Playwright MCP server's own npm version instead of floating on @latest (docs/agents/coding-conventions.md, 'Dependency maintenance'). That server browses untrusted prospect sites. Renovate reads/writes that pin the same way it would a package.json dependency.
Context7 MCP is pinned in .mcp.json so agent documentation behavior changes only through a reviewed diff.
IBM Equal Access CLI is pinned in the CI wrapper; Renovate keeps the secondary accessibility engine current through reviewed diffs.
The local Renovate runner pins its own image; Renovate reports its next version like any other dependency.
The restic Docker image is pinned in deployment scripts; Renovate keeps backup tooling updates reviewable.
